title: Choosing and Changing a TRICARE Prime Primary Care Manager
content:
Every active **TRICARE Prime** enrollee has exactly one primary care manager (PCM) at a time; a new assignment replaces the previous one from its effective date, and referrals already issued by the previous PCM stay valid until they expire. When an enrollment is activated, an initial PCM assignment is made for it, effective on the enrollment effective date.

## Conditions on an assignment

1. **Enrollment status.** PCM assignments are made only on an enrollment whose status is active, as the enrollment record shows.
2. **Setting.** The PCM's provider kind must be one of the settings the tier allows (military hospital or clinic, network primary care provider, or non-network participating provider, as listed for the tier).
3. **Service area.** The chosen PCM's service area must be the enrollee's residence service area, unless a signed access-standard waiver for that PCM is on file. The provider's service area, panel status and kind are read from the provider record; the residence service area from the enrollee's record; the waiver from the enrollee's PCM records.
4. **Pediatrics.** A provider whose specialty is pediatrics may serve as PCM only for an enrollee whose age on the effective date does not exceed the tier's pediatric age limit.

## Who chooses

- Active duty service members are assigned to a military hospital or clinic PCM by their unit and the military clinic, and a beneficiary request alone cannot move them to a network PCM.
- Every other enrollee may choose any network primary care provider whose panel is open, and may change PCM at any time without stating a reason; a change takes effect under the tier's PCM change rule.
- A military hospital or clinic PCM requested by a tier whose military PCM needs the facility's capacity approval is a request to that facility, recorded as an intake and decided by the facility in order of access priority group.
- When a PCM leaves the network or closes the panel, the region reassigns the enrollee and records the reason accordingly.

## Access-standard waivers

A waiver may be signed only by tiers that allow it, only by the enrollee (or the sponsor or legal guardian for a minor), covers only the named PCM, and lapses when that PCM assignment ends.

| PCM's service area is the residence service area | Signed waiver for that PCM on file | Service-area condition met |
|---|---|---|
| yes | not needed | yes |
| no | yes | yes |
| no | no | no |

## Boundary case on age (hypothetical, a tier whose pediatric age limit is 17)

An enrollee aged 17 in completed years on the effective date may have a pediatrics PCM; an enrollee who turned 18 before the effective date may not.
